beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The hard part is not access; it is absorption.
beats.got: Buying the tool is the easy part. Getting people to use it is the hard part, and that is what my programmes have always failed on.

beats.trigger: Walk in with one example where people had access to a tool or process but real use did not follow.
beats.got: I have plenty of examples. The ERP module nobody opened is one.

beats.trigger: **Interview** for your teammate's job-to-be-done using the agentic Jobs-to-be-Done pattern (Clayton Christensen and collaborators)
beats.got: Nothing I can price. It is a list of verbs, and there is no payback or cost figure anywhere.

beats.trigger: who's the one person who came to mind just now? And what makes you hesitate about actually handing this to them?
beats.got: Nothing new. It is a feelings question, and I do not have a Module 2-6 agent system to hand to anyone.

beats.trigger: Your teammate doesn't want your agent. They want a job done.
beats.got: The framing is to start from the job, not the tool. That is sensible, but 25 minutes is a lot of my day.

beats.trigger: If it could describe anyone in the room, point to the generic line and ask the agent to try that part again.
beats.got: The agent writes a document and I check whether it is specific. It would matter more if it were my own reports.

beats.trigger: *"Share the whole agent"* is a vendor pitch and is NOT on the list.
beats.got: There are four ways to share, and selling it as a licence is a vendor pitch. I like that it says so up front.

beats.trigger: You now have the teammate's job and a candidate selected against it.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Now find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can actually absorb it, then draft both halves of the plan.
beats.got: A technical plan and a people plan, with the obstacle found first.

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: Look for the one root cause, not a list of issues. That is how I read a P&L variance.

beats.trigger: Missing names remain visible as `UNASSIGNED — Monday's question`; the agent does not invent them.
beats.got: The tool flags what is not owned and does not make up an owner. That is how a risk register ought to work.

beats.trigger: checks the assumptions underneath these plans, imagines the failure, and writes the first real-world contact
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: The plans are hypotheses to test. Fine, but where is the budget line?

beats.trigger: what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?
beats.got: It is a decent test of whether anyone will switch. A business case should answer the same thing.

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.
beats.got: This is a pre-mortem, and it ends with one named person and one test. I can use that without being told to feel anything.

beats.trigger: A candidate picked because it fits the infrastructure is shopping.
beats.got: Pick the tool for the outcome, not for the platform we already own. That one I can defend to the board.

beats.trigger: The rest of this is about the person on the other end of your plan.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The outcome sentence is the contract: minimize or increase something, while doing that job.
beats.got: State the outcome as a measurable change. Good, though it still has no figures.

beats.trigger: They run it, get a generic answer, and quietly stop.
beats.got: A copied agent file gives a worse result without the owner's context, and nobody complains about it. That explains why our licences sit idle.

beats.trigger: Accountability is the part with a name on it, and a name does not travel inside a folder.
beats.got: The thing that does not copy is the person who answers for the result. I would ask the same of any investment.

beats.trigger: The two get reported as one number and they are not one thing.
beats.got: Seats bought and seats actually used get reported as one figure. That is the reason programmes never reach the P&L.

beats.trigger: Michael Polanyi, a philosopher of science, had the line for it: *we know more than we can tell.*
beats.got: Nothing new. A philosopher quote with no number attached.

beats.trigger: In the full agent picture, this is the interface piece.
beats.got: nothing new. It refers to a picture from earlier modules that I did not see.

beats.trigger: The leadership had not done the analysis. People they trusted had.
beats.got: Fifteen people did good work and the leadership gave no decision, because the leadership had not done the analysis themselves. I have been in that meeting, and it was the first part today I recognised.

beats.trigger: Somebody they trust has to have used it first and said so.
beats.got: The new tool has to beat the spreadsheet they already use, and it has to land where they already look.

beats.trigger: Whether they pick it up is their decision, made for their own reasons, on a Tuesday you will not be in the room for.
beats.got: Adoption is not in your control. Fair, but that is not a lot to build on.

beats.trigger: A missing name is a finding: it marks the part of this that is not built yet
beats.got: An empty owner field is the finding. I can use that as a test on any project that comes to me for budget.

beats.trigger: The agent reviews, rewrites the sharing artifact in place, and reports what changed.
beats.got: The agent tidies its own deliverable and I read the summary. That is process, not content.

beats.trigger: Push back where the agent's summary is wrong.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Access is easy; absorption is scarce.
beats.got: The four points are short enough that I could repeat them to my controller.

beats.trigger: Test one assumption. Ask for one name. Talk to one person.
beats.got: Homework is one conversation with one person. It is small enough that I might actually do it.

beats.trigger: What comes back from that contact is Module 8's raw material.
beats.got: nothing new

take_homes: Seats bought and people actually using the tool are two different numbers. If I only see access reported, I am not seeing adoption.
If a plan has no named owner for the result, treat that as the finding. The missing name tells me more than the technical plan does.
Choose the tool for the outcome, not because we already own the platform.

monday.move: Ask my controller who actually uses the three tools we already pay for in finance, and how she does month-end variance commentary today. Only after that would I ask whether she would try an agent on it.
monday.when: Monday morning, in the 15 minutes before the leadership meeting
monday.stop_condition: If she says the tools are used and the current method already works, I stop and do nothing more.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, and I still have no cost figure per user.

misconception.why: The module showed that buying access does not mean the organisation uses it, and that someone has to be accountable for the result. That is close to the line between a licence and a capability. Nobody gave a cost or a payback figure, so I only half accept it.

one_line: The two-day workshop story and the line about accountability not travelling with the folder were worth hearing, but I never saw a cost, a payback or a number, so I could not take it to the board.
